description: Cross-registry resolution MUST bind the retrieved body to the ctx_id that was requested. Per RFC-ACDP-0006 §4.1 step 7, `body.ctx_id` MUST equal the `ctx_id` used to construct the request URI in step 4 — a check that signature verification (step 5) and content_hash recomputation (step 6) cannot supply, because `ctx_id` is in the RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.7 registry-assigned exclusion set and is therefore stripped from ProducerContent before hashing. `GET /contexts/<encoded ctx_id A>` returns a body whose `ctx_id` is B; A and B share the same `agent_id`, and B's signature and content_hash BOTH verify correctly — that is the whole point: a resolver relying solely on steps 5 and 6 would accept this response and attribute body B to identity A.

input.scenario: Resolver requests GET https://registry.example.com/contexts/<encoded ctx_id A>; the registry (compromised, buggy, or malicious) instead returns a fully valid body whose body.ctx_id is B, a different context minted for the same agent_id. B's producer signature verifies against B's content_hash, and recomputing content_hash over B's JCS-canonicalized ProducerContent (with the RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.7 exclusion set stripped) matches — both step 5 and step 6 PASS. Only the new step 7 comparison of body.ctx_id (B) against the requested ctx_id (A) detects the substitution.

additional_test_cases.note: The response carries no registry_receipt at all — the acdp-rs #189 shape. RFC-ACDP-0010 §8's receipt-path binding does not apply because there is no receipt to check. The §4.1 step 7 comparison is the ONLY thing standing between the consumer and misattribution, which is exactly why the erratum makes it unconditional rather than leaving it implicit in the receipt path.

The response DOES carry a registry_receipt, but the receipt attests ctx_id B (the body actually returned) rather than the requested ctx_id A — a self-consistent receipt for the wrong body. RFC-ACDP-0010 §8 step 3 (receipt.ctx_id MUST equal the requested ctx_id) catches this FIRST and independently, verdict invalid_receipt. The new §4.1 step 7 check MUST ALSO independently fail on the same body/ctx_id comparison. A consumer MUST NOT treat a successful receipt check as a substitute for the unconditional step-7 check, and MUST NOT treat a failing receipt check as a substitute for step 7 either — both verdicts are produced and reported.

The requested ctx_id and body.ctx_id are compared as parsed acdp:// URIs (authority + UUID), never as raw strings. Two forms that MUST NOT be treated as a mismatch: (1) percent-encoding differences in the request path that decode to the identical authority+UUID; (2) the RFC-ACDP-0004 §2.1 path-style alternate retrieval form (GET /contexts/<authority>/<uuid>) versus the acdp://<authority>/<uuid> URI form — both resolve to the same context per RFC-ACDP-0004 §2.1 and MUST compare equal after parsing. A naive byte-compare of the raw request path against body.ctx_id would produce false failures on these equivalent forms.

expected.behavior: The resolver MUST compare the parsed acdp:// identity of body.ctx_id against the parsed acdp:// identity of the ctx_id used to construct the step-4 request URI. On mismatch, the resolver MUST treat the resolution as failed and surface cross_registry_resolution_failed (consumer-side: an equivalent typed error). The body MUST NOT be surfaced to the caller under the originally-requested identity, and MUST NOT be entered into a cache keyed by the requested ctx_id (RFC-ACDP-0006 §4.3) — content_hash validation on a cache read would not detect the substitution, because ctx_id sits outside the hashed ProducerContent.
expected.rationale: ctx_id is a registry-assigned field in the RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.7 exclusion set: it is stripped from ProducerContent before content_hash is computed, so it is covered by neither content_hash recomputation (RFC-ACDP-0006 §4.1 step 6) nor the producer signature (step 5), which signs only the hash. Without an explicit binding check, a registry — compromised, buggy, or malicious — can serve any other validly-signed body by the same producer under any other context's URL, and a resolver that stops at steps 5–6 will accept it and attribute the wrong content to the requested identity. Attributing the wrong body silently corrupts any evidence chain a derived_from walk later grafts onto that identity. RFC-ACDP-0010 §8 step 3 already requires this same binding when a registry receipt accompanies the response; this fixture pins the unconditional form so a receipt-less retrieval (the acdp-rs #189 gap) is not weaker.

additional_failure_cases.expected_outcome: The step 7 ctx_id-binding check still applies and still fails with cross_registry_resolution_failed; absence of a registry_receipt does not weaken or bypass the binding requirement.

additional_failure_cases.case: a receipt IS served but attests the returned (wrong) body
additional_failure_cases.expected_outcome: RFC-ACDP-0010 §8 step 3 catches the receipt/requested-ctx_id mismatch first and independently, verdict invalid_receipt. The §4.1 step 7 check MUST ALSO independently fail (cross_registry_resolution_failed) on the same underlying comparison. A consumer MUST NOT treat receipt verification success as a substitute for the unconditional step-7 check — the two checks are reported as distinct verdicts, not collapsed into one.

MUST NOT be treated as a mismatch. The comparison is over the parsed acdp:// URI (authority + UUID), not the raw request path string, so percent-encoding differences and the path-style alternate retrieval form (/contexts/<authority>/<uuid>) compare equal to the acdp://<authority>/<uuid> form when they denote the same context.
